Subject: Post-call recap: Tool/function-calling integration patterns & next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom (copying Tom who joined briefly),

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion on your ingestion and orchestration needs for FinApps' transaction categorization and enrichment flows. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our side: 

1) Goals we heard
- Low-latency enrichment for interactive UI (<300ms p99 ideal)
- Batch reprocessing for historical data with higher throughput
- Deterministic structured output for downstream consumers (ledger updates, reporting)

2) Recommended high-level integration patterns
- SDK setup & auth: Use Redwood SDK (server-side) with short-lived service tokens. For FinApps' security posture you can either use API keys rotated via your KMS or integrate OIDC-based short-lived tokens. If you need a private deployment, we can offer VPC/private control plane.
- Routing & model choices: Route latency-sensitive calls to smaller fast models (quantized variants) and heavy-lift batch requests to higher-quality variants. We recommend policy-based routing (by route / user tier) so you can prioritize interactive sessions.
- Tool/function calling & structured output: Prefer explicit tool definitions for deterministic outputs (e.g., "categorize_transaction", "fetch_merchant_metadata"). Tools should declare input schema and required fields; Redwood will validate and surface errors before calling downstream services.
- Embeddings & rerankers: Use embeddings for candidate retrieval, then run a lightweight reranker (BERT-ish) for final selection. Store embeddings in your vector DB; we can provide batched embedding endpoints for throughput efficiency.

3) Tool/function-calling integration patterns we discussed (summary)
- Tool definitions: Define tools with a strict JSON schema (inputs/outputs). Keep side-effects explicit and idempotent.
- Tool choice: Use a two-stage pipeline: retrieval -> candidate tool selection -> tool execution. Maintain a fallback (text-only generation) when tool execution fails.
- Parallel tools: Run independent enrichment tools in parallel (merchant_lookup, aml_check), but gate commits to the ledger until all mandatory checks pass or a safe fallback is chosen. Use per-tool timeouts and aggregate error handling.
- Error handling: Retries with exponential backoff for transient failures, deterministic fallbacks for business-critical calls, and circuit breakers for repeated downstream failures. Log structured error codes for observability.

4) Attachments
- Attached: redwood-tool-calling-patterns.pdf (best-practice patterns) and a sample integration diagram (integration-diagram.png).

Next steps / asks
- Can you share a short sample dataset (anonymized) or schema and expected throughput (rps for interactive, size of batch jobs)?
- Which auth model do you prefer (API keys/KMS vs OIDC short-lived tokens)?
- Can we schedule a 1-hr tech deep-dive next week with your engineering team to go over tool schemas and routing policies? We propose Tue/Wed next week.

I'll loop Alex and Dev for availability and to prepare a tailored architecture doc after we get the answers above.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Tom — a couple of clarifications from the engineering side and small proposed design decisions so the deep-dive is focused: 

- Tool schema: We'll share a sample JSON Schema for a "categorize_transaction" tool. Recommendation: keep outputs explicit (status, category_id, confidence, metadata). Redwood will perform a schema validation pass before invoking the tool to avoid downstream surprises.
- Parallel execution: For independent enrichment calls (merchant_lookup, risk_score, aml_check), run them as parallel async calls with a global deadline (e.g., 300ms) and individual tool timeouts (e.g., 120ms). If mandatory tools miss the deadline, we either (a) use cached results if <TTL or (b) fallback to a lightweight model-based approximation and flag for async recheck.
- Retries & idempotency: Tools with side-effects must accept an idempotency token from the platform. Retries will use this token to avoid double-commits.
- Error codes & observability: We'll emit structured error codes for retryable vs non-retryable and provide trace ids that correlate model calls to tool invocations in Redwood Console.

I've attached a lightweight example of the JSON Schema and an updated integration diagram. Happy to walk through on Wed 3/4 at 10am PT if that works for you.
